title: Compact full-B2 coefficient-four proof with a paid field prefix

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. For g(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee, liminf over all integer n of C_B2(f_n)/g(n) >= 1. Equivalently, for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(f_n)>=(1-epsilon)*g(n) for every integer n>=N_epsilon. Declaration: {"convention":"uniform-np-full-b2-actual-length-all-lengths-v1","family":"The single total certificate-prefix family defined at every length in proof.md Sections1--2 and family.py. Select the least prime k at least the least positive integer b with b^5>32N^3; put m=N-k, r=ceil(m/k), t=ceil(sqrt(r)), with the exact exceptional guards and d from proof.md. Read a paid k-bit irreducible-polynomial prefix, reject invalid prefixes, and evaluate the descending-power elementary symmetric payload polynomial of order t with zero padding.","guarantee":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"polynomial_log","log_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"},"loglog_exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"0"}},"projection":{"coefficient":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"4"},"exponent":{"denominator":"1","numerator":"1"},"kind":"finite"},"theorem":"This one fixed total language is in uniform P, hence NP with empty witnesses. At every sufficiently large actual integer input length N, all guards pass and C_B2(F_N)>=4N-(4k+8d), where 4k+8d=O(N^(4/5))=o(N). Therefore for every epsilon>0 there is N_epsilon such that C_B2(F_N)>=(4-epsilon)N for every integer N>=N_epsilon in the full Li-Yang B2 model.","version":"circuitbreaker-expression-v1"}
